tour.overview:
On the plateau between Cusco and the Sacred Valley, at about 3,500 metres, two of the most unusual sites of the Andes lie a few kilometres apart. At Moray, the Incas shaped natural sinkholes into giant amphitheatres of circular terraces up to 30 metres deep; the temperature varies by several degrees between the top and the bottom, and many researchers believe it served to acclimatise and improve crops. Below the village of Maras, a salty spring flows out of the mountain and is channelled into some 3,000 small evaporation pools, worked by local families as a cooperative since pre-Inca times.

This private half day explores both with a licensed guide and a car, with views of the snowy Urubamba range across the fields of the plateau. It combines well with Chinchero or the Sacred Valley.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 5 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Cusco or the Sacred Valley
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate; short walks at altitude

WHAT YOU SEE
• The circular terraces of Moray.
• The village of Maras.
• The Maras salt pans.
• The Urubamba range.

WHY THIS WORKS
The sites are far from public transport; with a car you see both in a few hours and can add Chinchero or end in the Sacred Valley.

WHO IT SUITS
Photographers, families and anyone with a spare half day in Cusco.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you want more Inca sites in one day, choose our Sacred Valley tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Visitors may no longer walk among the salt pans themselves; you see them from the marked paths. The salt pans are most photogenic from May to November, when they are full and white.

days.name: The circular terraces of Moray, the village of Maras and the salt pans
days.description:
What to expect: two extraordinary sites of the Andean plateau, with a licensed guide, private car and tickets.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at about 8:00 and drive across the plateau of Chinchero, among fields of potatoes, quinoa and barley, with the glaciers of the Urubamba range – Chicón, Verónica, Sahuasiray – on the horizon. At Moray you look down into the great circular depressions shaped by the Incas into rings of terraces, each with its own stone irrigation channels and stairways of flat stones jutting from the walls. Your guide explains why the temperature changes between the levels, how the site may have served to adapt crops from different altitudes, and the debates among archaeologists.

You drive through the colonial village of Maras, with its adobe houses and church, and down a dirt road to the salt pans. Across the side of a valley, about 3,000 shallow pools step down the slope like a white and ochre mosaic, fed by a warm, salty spring that emerges from the mountain. Families of the local community each own a few pools, which they flood with brine and leave to evaporate, then scrape to harvest salt, the pink salt being prized by chefs. You follow the marked path above the pools and can buy salt directly from the producers. You are back at your hotel at about 13:00, or your driver can drop you in the Sacred Valley.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:00 – Pick-up at your hotel.
09:15 – Moray.
10:45 – Maras village.
11:15 – Maras salt pans.
13:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Chinchero can be added for a full day.
• An easy hike or mountain-bike ride from Moray to the salt pans can be arranged.
• The salt pans are inactive or flooded in the rainy season, from December to April.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, tickets, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Are the tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: Moray (part of the tourist ticket) and the Maras salt pans entrance.

faq.question: Can we walk among the salt pans?
faq.answer: No longer: to protect the pools, visitors stay on the marked paths and viewpoints.

faq.question: Can we combine it with other sites?
faq.answer: Yes. Chinchero, the Sacred Valley or an afternoon train to Machu Picchu from Ollantaytambo combine easily.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love tasting the salt and looking down into the giant terraces. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. Both sites have viewpoints near the car park; the paths into Moray and along the salt pans are uneven.

faq.question: Is the altitude a problem?
faq.answer: The plateau is at about 3,500 metres. Walk slowly and drink water.

faq.question: Can we buy salt?
faq.answer: Yes, directly from the families who produce it, at the salt pans.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Peru but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Layers, sun protection, a hat and comfortable shoes.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: May to November, when the salt pans are full and the skies clear.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
